definition: Daisy Intelligence is a Canadian artificial intelligence (AI) company that provides data analysis services to help retailers, mainly grocers and supermarkets, to determine optimal pricing and promotional mix.
details: The company also helps insurance companies detect fraudulent claims. The company uses a subset of AI known as reinforcement learning. In October 2019, the company moved from the suburban Vaughan, Ontario, to downtown Toronto, joining other AI and technology startups concentrated in the King Street East area. In 2019, the company was ranked No. 39 on The Globe and Mail's annual list of Canada's "top growing companies by three-year revenue growth."

explainer.lead: Daisy Intelligence is a Canadian AI company that helps retailers choose prices and promotions, with a particular focus on grocers and supermarkets. It also applies its data-analysis services to detecting fraudulent insurance claims.

tiers.eli5: Choosing a price or a sale is a bit like trying different moves in a game and learning which ones work well. Daisy Intelligence uses this kind of learning to help grocery stores decide on prices and promotions. It also helps insurance companies spot claims that may be fraudulent.
tiers.practitioner: Daisy Intelligence is applied as a decision-support service for retail pricing, promotional mix, and insurance claim-fraud detection. Its retail work uses reinforcement learning, so teams should distinguish action-and-feedback optimization from ordinary demand forecasting. Outputs still need operational review rather than being treated as guaranteed optimal decisions or proof of fraud.
tiers.paperLevel: The company frames part of its approach as reinforcement learning: an agent selects actions and uses outcome feedback to improve its decision policy. The application objectives include optimizing retail pricing and promotional mix, alongside fraudulent-claim detection in insurance. No specific architecture, reward function, or performance results are established in the available description.

explainer.example: A supermarket could use Daisy Intelligence’s analysis to compare candidate prices and promotional combinations, then select a mix for its products instead of choosing every discount manually.
